write(2) takes a file descriptor, an address and a count. Which descriptor does your call hand it, the one your function was given or another, and how many bytes does it ask for, for one character?
Is a NUL written like any other character, or does something in your code treat it differently? Compare the row of the NUL byte with the others.
A char can hold the byte 0xff: what value does a plain char holding it have on this machine, and does anything your code does with c change the byte that reaches the file?
The last row calls your function 256 times, once for each value a char holds. Does every call write exactly one byte, the one it was given, whatever came before it?
